P56.best: 5F work booths are the quiet option and often near-empty; the 4F cafe booths fill by 09:00 on weekdays with people on calls.
P56.workNotes: Card entry at the ground-floor door; 4F allows phone calls and eating, 5F allows neither; partitioned single booths and sofa seats; free printer; loan monitors are scarce.
P56.headsUp: One unisex toilet on 5F with queues; a shaky old lift; two 2026 reviews complain of body odour on 4F and a 2024 one of cup-noodle smells. Drop-in pricing is not published.

why.vibe: A 2.9-star floor with smell complaints, a frightening lift and a single shared toilet.
why.uniq: Standard BIZcomfort chain fit-out with nothing to set it apart.
why.food: A drinks corner on 4F is all that is mentioned.
why.work: 24-hour access and partitioned desks, but a full 4F by morning, few monitors and unpublished drop-in terms.

quotes.text: 4階は電話会議可能、5階は会議、食事不可。
4階は匂いが汗臭く場所を移っても同じだと思ったので10分といられなかったです。
トイレは5Fのみ。男女兼用
カフェブース縮小により平日は朝9時から満席状態に。

P56.summaryEn: A split verdict at 2.9 stars: the location, partitions and free printer are appreciated, but reviewers report smells, a scary lift, a single shared toilet, too few monitors, a full 4F by morning and noisy eaters.

P57.pitch: Beach-themed basement coworking by Shibuya's new south exit: wave soundtrack, free drinks, borrowable monitors and a sociable events crowd; day rate only.
order: Free drink server (contents not confirmed)
P57.best: Full days, since there is no hourly rate. Check the current schedule first: Google now shows weekdays 10:00-21:00 and closed at weekends, and a mid-2026 review mentions a renovation period.
P57.workNotes: Open floor allows conversation, phone and web calls; soundproof TEL booths are free but booking-only; monitors and gadgets lent free; registration runs through LINE and one visitor found it slow. First visit is half price if you show the website.
P57.headsUp: Hours are in flux: the listing says 9-22 daily, Google says weekdays only, and the space may be mid-refit. Cool white lighting and the longer walk from the Hachiko side put some off.

why.vibe: Wave sounds, considerate regulars and staff who act on feedback; a 4.7 rating across 89 reviews backs it up.
why.uniq: A beach concept with an events programme in a Shibuya basement is a genuinely distinct idea.
why.food: A free drink server and nothing else stated.
why.work: Calls allowed, free booths and gadgets; day-only pricing and uncertain opening days are the catch.

quotes.text: 波のBGMがこんなにも心地良いなんて。
最新機器が利用し放題、ドリンクも飲み放題。
いまはリニューアル期間中？
ドロップインは1デイのみの3300円（時間単位があれば...）

P57.summaryEn: Strong 4.7 rating: clean, friendly staff who act on surveys, free gadgets and drinks, and a calm floor outside event hours; the few grumbles are day-only pricing, LINE sign-up, cool lighting and distance from the main exits.

P58.pitch: Bare-bones 7F coworking by the new south exit charging a flat ¥1,000 a day; self-styled cheapest in Shibuya, with reviews that stop in 2019.
order: Drinks: not confirmed
P58.best: Listed 10:00-19:00 including weekends; nothing recent enough to say when it is quiet.
P58.workNotes: Wi-Fi confirmed by a 2015 reviewer and Aeron chairs by another; outlets, booths, call rules and registration are not documented.
P58.headsUp: Google shows no hours and the newest review is from 2019, so confirm it still operates before going; the phone reportedly goes unanswered, and older reviews describe loud resident tenants.

why.vibe: A 2.9-star office floor whose most vivid review is about a rowdy tenant company.
why.uniq: The only idea is being the cheapest; otherwise an anonymous rental floor.
why.food: Nothing on drinks or food anywhere in the record.
why.work: Wi-Fi and good chairs at a bargain rate, but 19:00 close, no hours on Google and no recent evidence it is open.

quotes.text: とにかく電話が繋がらないです。。。
ドロップインの料金も使いやすい価格帯です。
アーロンチェアあり

P58.summaryEn: Eight old reviews: cheap and usable on weekends, Aeron chairs, but a noisy contracted crowd and a phone nobody answers; nothing since 2019.

P59.pitch: Resonance's members-first Shibuya point with hexagonal dedicated desks and a six-seat private room; drop-in is not advertised, so ask before turning up.
order: Drinks: not confirmed
P59.best: Reception is staffed 10:00-18:00 while the floor is listed as open 6:00-22:00, so a first visit belongs inside reception hours.
P59.workNotes: Free small-volume printing, hexagonal fixed desks, a six-person private room and hourly meeting rooms per the listing; outlets, Wi-Fi and call rules are not documented.
P59.headsUp: No Google listing matched and there are no reviews; the listing does not confirm drop-in at all. Treat it as a rental-desk operation until told otherwise.

why.vibe: Nothing to judge beyond a tidy listing; assumed clean and unremarkable.
why.uniq: Hexagonal dedicated desks are at least a specific idea.
why.food: No drinks or food mentioned anywhere.
why.work: Printing and rooms exist, but no confirmed drop-in, no Wi-Fi or outlet evidence and reception closes at 18:00.

P59.summaryEn: No recent Google reviews to draw on.

P60.pitch: Tsutaya's all-inclusive lounge over Shibuya Crossing: unlimited snacks, soft drinks and alcohol on the clock, plus outlets, magazines and meeting rooms.
order: Unlimited snacks, soft drinks and alcohol included
Frozen meals (often sold out by mid-morning)
P60.best: Window seats over the crossing are the draw and go first; one reviewer calls it never too crowded. Google says it opens 08:00, so mornings are the calm stretch.
P60.workNotes: Outlets at every seat, stable Wi-Fi, bookable rooms suited to online meetings; online booking and tablet check-in with no lengthy registration; over 100 magazines free to read.
P60.headsUp: Sources disagree on the address (Scramble Square 11F versus Tsutaya 4F) and on price, which has risen; regulars complain the lounge shrank to one floor with thinner snack and frozen-food stock.

why.vibe: Modern, clean and comfortable with the crossing below the window; foreign visitors rave, locals grumble about decline.
why.uniq: Unlimited snacks and alcohol billed by the hour above Shibuya Crossing is its own thing.
why.food: Snacks, drinks and alcohol are real, but stock runs thin and frozen meals sell out early.
why.work: Outlets everywhere, Wi-Fi, meeting rooms and 08-23 hours; the price makes a full day an expensive habit.

quotes.text: ネットで予約ができ、タブレットでチェックインできるので凄く簡単にできてびっくりしました！
スナックの量や冷凍食品の品揃えが減っていて大変残念
午前10時半に行ったら全部品切れで、食べられませんでした。

P60.summaryEn: Tourists and remote workers praise the view, clean modern room, easy booking and the unlimited food-and-drink concept; Japanese regulars complain of price rises, a shrunken footprint and snacks or frozen meals running out early.

signals.crowding: never too crowded, per one review

P61.pitch: Two JR phone-booth pods inside Shibuya's Shin-Minami ticket gate: a monitor, a socket and air-con for a 15-minute call between trains.
order: Nothing; bring a drink from the concourse
P61.best: Use it as intended: a call or a quick edit while changing trains, 07:00-21:30. Only two pods, so commuter peaks may find both taken.
P61.workNotes: Free power, Wi-Fi and an HDMI monitor in a sealed single booth; billed per 15 minutes; one source says walk-in without registration or booking works.
P61.headsUp: You need to be inside the JR gates; the pod is tight for larger builds, and the rate rose from ¥275 to ¥330 in May 2025.

why.vibe: A sealed pod on a station concourse; functional and nothing more.
why.uniq: A rentable booth inside the ticket gate is a distinct idea, even if JR has planted them everywhere.
why.food: Nothing inside; concourse kiosks only.
why.work: Power, Wi-Fi and a monitor, but 15-minute billing, two pods and no room to spread out.

P61.summaryEn: No recent Google reviews to draw on.

P62.pitch: Nex's THE HUB rental-office floors on Shibuya 3-chome with a cheap by-the-half-hour drop-in: silent 4F, talkative 5F, drinks and weekday snacks.
order: Free drink server (coffee, tea)
Free snacks on weekdays; not restocked over holidays
P62.best: Weekends and holidays leave the silent 4F almost empty, which suits exam study if you can stand the solitude; weekdays are busier on the conversational 5F.
P62.workNotes: Outlets and Wi-Fi throughout, loan monitors, bookable phone booths and a free meeting corner; calls and eating on 5F, silence on 4F. Entry and exit only while reception is staffed, so mind the lunch break; hours are weekdays 10-19 per one source and 7-23 daily per Google.
P62.headsUp: No day cap, so a long day adds up; tables are cleaned by users with wet wipes and can be grubby; over long holidays the drink server may sit empty.

why.vibe: Clean, simple office floors that reviewers find pleasant; grubby tables are the only knock on the room.
why.uniq: A standard rental-office chain with a drop-in tier bolted on.
why.food: Free drinks and weekday snacks, unreliably restocked.
why.work: Outlets, Wi-Fi, monitors, booths and a silent floor at a low rate; staffed-hours-only access and no day cap are the limits.

quotes.text: 5分刻みの30分単位で利用できて、料金も安くて使いやすかったです。
土日祝日はめちゃくちゃ人が少ない。
ドリンクサーバーの中身が補充されず、何も飲めないことも珍しくありません。
自習室が相次いで閉業している渋谷エリアではおそらく最もコスパの高い場所ではあると思います。

P62.summaryEn: Reviewers call it the best value study desk left in Shibuya: cheap increments, easy booth booking, monitors and drinks; downsides are grubby tables, empty drink servers over holidays and a deserted quiet floor at weekends.

signals.crowding: 5F busier on weekdays; 4F near-empty at weekends

P63.pitch: coin space's flagship inside Mark City West 4F, sharing a door with the tourist office; no registration, ten-minute billing, calls allowed.
order: Water server only; bring your own food and drink
P63.best: Mornings, when one reviewer found it empty enough for a web call; the day cap is ¥2,500 until 19:00, then a separate ¥1,500 night cap to 23:00.
P63.workNotes: Outlets at all 44 seats, Wi-Fi, free phone-charger loan, monitors for ¥500; web and phone calls permitted; individual booths and counter seats; walk in with no sign-up.
P63.headsUp: Dearer than other branches and dearer than a cafe over a full day; the entrance doubles as the Shibuya tourist association counter, with the desks up a flight of stairs.

why.vibe: White, bright and clean, but small and tucked behind a tourist information counter.
why.uniq: A chain coin-op floor whose only quirk is the shared tourist-office entrance.
why.food: A water server and permission to bring your own.
why.work: Every seat has power, calls are fine and hours run 9-23; the size and the full-day cost are the limitations.

quotes.text: 10分110円、安くていいですね。
事前の面倒な手続きがなく、ふらっとドロップインできる手軽さも助かります。
登録不要で使えるのが最大の強みで

P63.summaryEn: Praised for location, no-fuss walk-in, full outlets and call-friendly rules; noted as small and pricier than other branches, better for an hour or two than a whole day.

P64.pitch: Cafe-styled 5F coworking opposite PARCO with a wide view over Shibuya; weekday-only hourly drop-in, friendly staff, water but no coffee.
order: Water server; one listing claims free drinks but a regular reports water only
P64.best: The big central table is the one to work at; the low sofa tables strain the back. Weekdays 10:00-19:00 only.
P64.workNotes: Outlets at every seat plus loan power strips; Wi-Fi was weak in 2024 but fixed by 2025; two bookable meeting rooms usually free; registration is quick.
P64.headsUp: Closed Saturday and Sunday and shuts at 19:00. One review objects to communal cups being rinsed and reused and to a grimy copier corner.

why.vibe: A 4.7 rating over 152 reviews, mostly about the view and a clean, comfortable room.
why.uniq: Cafe-style seating with a panoramic outlook is a distinct pitch among Shibuya's office floors.
why.food: A water server and nothing else, whatever the listing says.
why.work: All-seat outlets, fixed Wi-Fi and meeting rooms; weekday 10-19 hours and low tables hold it back.

quotes.text: 渋谷の街並みを一望できて快適な空間
真ん中のでっかいテーブルが一番作業しやすい。
ウォーターサーバーがあります！
コピー機周辺が汚い。

P64.summaryEn: Overwhelmingly positive: the view, clean room, easy sign-up, fair price and helpful staff; caveats are low tables awkward for laptops, a past Wi-Fi wobble and one complaint about hygiene.

P65.pitch: Airline-lounge styled members' club on the 17th floor of Fukuras, terrace included; polished for client meetings, awkward for a casual drop-in.
order: Drinks: not confirmed
P65.best: Sunday 10:00-18:00 is the odd bonus, since Saturday is closed; the terrace and even the toilet corridor give the view. Bring earphones for a call-heavy floor.
P65.workNotes: Booth seats at no extra charge, and outlets plus Wi-Fi even on the terrace; weekday hours run to 21:00 or 22:00 depending on source. The listing says both no drop-in and ¥3,300 all-day, so ring ahead.
P65.headsUp: Closed Saturdays; only two lifts serve the floor so queues form; contracted companies dominate and one visitor felt like a squatter in someone else's office.

why.vibe: High-floor views, a terrace and a weighty finish that reviewers say impresses clients.
why.uniq: The airport-lounge conceit with uniformed reception is a recognisable idea, if a slightly silly one.
why.food: Nothing about drinks or food in the record.
why.work: Outlets and Wi-Fi even outdoors, but a Saturday closure, constant callers and contradictory drop-in terms.

quotes.text: 土曜日が定休日なのが最大の欠点。
17階なので眺めがいいです。
ドロップインで気軽に利用するオープンな雰囲気ではないと感じました。
通話の人が結構が多いので、イヤホンとかないと集中できないのでは。

P65.summaryEn: The view, terrace and business-lounge finish earn praise for client meetings; complaints are the Saturday closure, crowded lifts, constant phone calls and a members-only feel that leaves drop-ins uneasy.

P66.pitch: Regus serviced offices on the 16th and 22nd floors of Mark City West; a lounge with a Shibuya view for tenants and their guests, not a walk-in desk.
order: Drinks: not confirmed
P66.best: Weekdays 09:00-18:00 only, and only with a membership or a booked meeting room; the lounge view is the reason tenants stay.
P66.workNotes: Rental offices, two meeting rooms and a members' lounge; the listing says no drop-in, so outlets, Wi-Fi and call rules are moot for a visitor.
P66.headsUp: Not a drop-in venue; the listing says so outright. One 2026 review alleges a deposit unreturned after 40 days, and another found the entrance hard to find.

why.vibe: Spacious, high up, station-linked and staffed; tenants describe a genuinely nice place to bring clients.
why.uniq: A Regus centre is the definition of a generic chain floor.
why.food: Nothing on drinks or food in the record.
why.work: Office-hours only and closed to walk-ins; usable only as a member or meeting-room booker.

quotes.text: 眺望よく来客の方にも喜んでいただき、ラウンジや会議室で気持ちよく仕事ができます。
とにかく広い。渋谷駅直通のためフレキシブルに公私を分けられる。
着手金が40日以上経っても返金されない。

P66.summaryEn: Tenants like the view, space, station link and staffed reception; the low scores are about contract money not being refunded and a confusing entrance.

P67.pitch: Small coworking floor run by a virtual-office operator near Tower Records; cheap half-hour billing and a phone box, but office hours only.
order: Drinks: not confirmed
P67.best: Weekdays 09:00-18:00 and nothing else; both reviewers wanted evenings and weekends and did not get them.
P67.workNotes: Phone box and bookable meeting room; business registration available; outlets and Wi-Fi not documented in the brief; the floor is described as not large.
P67.headsUp: Shut evenings and weekends; one reviewer found reception brusque. Only two reviews, so thin evidence.

why.vibe: Described as usable and no more; a small office floor at three stars.
why.uniq: A virtual-office firm's side desk; nothing distinctive.
why.food: No drinks or food mentioned.
why.work: A phone box and a day cap, but 9-18 weekday hours and no evidence on outlets or Wi-Fi.

quotes.text: コワーキングスペースは使いやすいですが、会議室も含めて土日も利用できると有難い。
土日も使えたらよかったです。

P67.summaryEn: Two three-star reviews: the desks are fine, but both users want weekend and evening opening and one found reception could be more courteous.

P68.pitch: Kaikatsu CLUB net cafe on floors 2-4 of a Center-gai building: locked private booths, drink bar and soft-serve, 24 hours, at central-Shibuya prices.
order: Free drink bar and soft-serve ice cream
P68.best: Off-peak weekday daytime for a booth with a door; check the app for vacancies but expect it to be wrong on busy nights.
P68.workNotes: Locked private rooms with Wi-Fi and power; membership card and ID on first visit as at every Kaikatsu branch; copier and towel loan on site.
P68.headsUp: Fridays are billed at the holiday rate, which surprised one reviewer with ¥1,220 for under an hour; the app has shown vacancies when there were none; the manga shelf is thin.

why.vibe: Clean and well kept, but a windowless net-cafe cubicle at 3.4 stars is still a cubicle.
why.uniq: A standard Kaikatsu floor; the private-room format is the chain's, not this branch's.
why.food: Free drink bar and soft-serve; the chain's food menu is not confirmed in the record.
why.work: A lockable room with power and Wi-Fi around the clock; the weekend-and-Friday pricing is the limitation.

quotes.text: 金曜日は休日料金なんで！
綺麗でドリンクバーやソフトクリームもあり、バスタオル貸出付で
利用時間の割に料金が高すぎる。
アプリで空室確認し来店したが空室無し。

P68.summaryEn: Clean, well staffed, with drink bar, soft-serve and towels for overnighters; the loud complaint is price, higher than other Kaikatsu branches with Fridays billed as holidays, plus an unreliable vacancy app.

P69.pitch: Sixth-floor Basis Point branch a minute from Jimbocho A5; quarter-hour billing, drink bar, calls allowed, for anyone needing a quiet desk for a few hours.
order: Free drink bar
Water server
Bring your own food (allowed)
P69.best: Weekday mornings from 08:00 before the room fills; reviewers like being able to pick a seat type, and the 1-4 person box seats (¥1,980/h) suit calls.
P69.workNotes: Outlets at every seat, fast Wi-Fi, chargers lent at reception; talking allowed everywhere and web meetings fine with earphones; leave-and-return permitted, day rate kicks in after 3.5 hours; open seats bookable, one free trial day offered.
P69.headsUp: Weekends open later at 10:00; closed over New Year. Reception is on 6F, so allow a minute for the lift.

why.vibe: Nearly every recent review says calm, clean and quiet, with smart interiors.
why.uniq: A well-run but standard chain floor; the seat-type choice is the only real flourish.
why.food: Free drink bar and a water server, nothing more; bring-in food is allowed.
why.work: Outlets everywhere, fast Wi-Fi, calls permitted, 08:00-22:00 weekdays and a fair day cap.

quotes.text: 室内がとても綺麗で静かなので集中できます。
充電器の貸し出しが大変助かりました。
駅からも近く内装もおしゃれ、Wi-Fi電源もあり、集中して作業するには最適の場所です。

P69.summaryEn: Reviews (4.4, 270) are uniformly positive: quiet, clean, close to the station, with charger loans and a water server singled out; no substantive complaints in the sample.

P70.pitch: Independent lawn-themed coworking lounge between Ochanomizu and Akihabara; cheap hourly desks and free private booths, suits solo workers wanting quiet.
order: Café area on site (details not confirmed)
P70.best: Hours are 10:00-18:00 every day, so this is a daytime room; booths go by reservation first, so ask for one on arrival.
P70.workNotes: Private booths included in the price but reservation takes priority; café area, lounge and meeting rooms on the floor; Wi-Fi and outlets not stated in this sheet but reported at the sister listing.
P70.headsUp: Closes at 18:00 sharp. This appears to be the same operator (and probably the same 7F room) as the Akihabara GrinSpace listing, whose source quotes a lower ¥1,650 day rate; check the website before paying.

why.vibe: Green, lawn-styled interior sounds pleasant, but no reviews attach to this listing.
why.uniq: The lawn-and-shoes-off idea is a genuine concept in a district of grey office floors.
why.food: A café area is claimed but what is served is unconfirmed.
why.work: Free booths and a cheap day rate, but 18:00 closing rules out evening work.

P70.summaryEn: No recent Google reviews to draw on.

P71.pitch: Three-floor LEAGUE workspace on Yasukuni-dori with a 9,000-book library; walk-in day pass with no registration, best for readers and quiet solo work.
order: Lounge café: coffee and sweets
P71.best: The only reviewer comes to read novels end to end on the sofa cushions; weekday hours run 09:00-20:00, Saturdays finish at 18:00.
P71.workNotes: Drop-in needs no registration or booking; lounge café, meeting rooms, dedicated desks and private offices up to 16 people; outlets and Wi-Fi not stated in the sheet.
P71.headsUp: Google lists Sunday closed and Saturday 10:00-18:00, against the sheet claim of weekends to 19:00 with no closing day. Day pass only, no hourly rate.

why.vibe: Sofas, cushions and walls of books; the one review treats it as a reading room.
why.uniq: A coworking space built around a 9,000-volume library is a distinct proposition.
why.food: A lounge café serving coffee and sweets rather than a drink bar.
why.work: No hourly pricing, Sunday closure and unconfirmed outlets hold it below a full 5.

quotes.text: 落ち着いて　良質なソファークッションで　読書に最適。
本に囲まれて、時折、甘味やコーヒーを。

P71.summaryEn: Only two Google reviews (4.5); the sampled one praises the sofa cushions and books for long reading sessions, with coffee and sweets on hand.

P72.pitch: Startup-oriented shared office on the 8-9F of a Suidobashi tower; stylish lounge and desk area with free drinks, suits founders and remote workers on a weekday.
order: Free drink bar
Bring your own food
P72.best: Drop-in runs weekdays 10:00-18:00 only; the lounge is the nicer end of the floor and reviewers found it calm.
P72.workNotes: Fast Wi-Fi and outlets at every seat, online-meeting booths, several bookable meeting rooms from ¥2,200/h; staff described as helpful.
P72.headsUp: Google shows 24 hours but that is member access; visitors get 10:00-18:00 weekdays with irregular closures. One lift serves the building, so expect a wait at the ground floor.

why.vibe: Reviewers call the interior tasteful and calm.
why.uniq: A well-finished but conventional startup shared office.
why.food: Free drinks only.
why.work: Outlets, Wi-Fi and booths are all there, but drop-in hours end at 18:00 on weekdays only.

quotes.text: エレベーターが一つだけなのが不便。
センス良い空間で落ち着いて仕事ができます。
おしゃれな内装で落ち着いた雰囲気で仕事に集中できた。

P72.summaryEn: Three reviews (4.3), none newer than 2023: stylish, calm, helpful staff and bookable meeting rooms; the single complaint is the lone elevator.

P73.pitch: Toyota-group innovation hub in Kanda-Ogawamachi with a flat ¥1,650 all-day desk, web-meeting booths and an event space; suits people who want a cheap full day.
order: Drinks: not confirmed
P73.best: Google lists weekdays 09:00-22:00 and Saturday to 18:00, so a weekday evening is the widest window; the sheet claims 09:00-18:00, so confirm before planning a late session.
P73.workNotes: Fast Wi-Fi and outlets at each seat, dedicated web-conference booths; day pass only, no hourly rate; event space shares the floor.
P73.headsUp: Closed Sundays. Run as a corporate innovation space, so expect events and an office-visitor feel rather than café informality.

why.vibe: The one sampled review calls it a creative, inspiring room, but 4.0 across 23 reviews suggests a solid rather than special floor.
why.uniq: A Toyota-group hub that sells day passes to the public is an unusual arrangement.
why.food: Nothing about drinks in the claims or reviews.
why.work: Booths, outlets and Wi-Fi at a low flat rate; Sunday closure and hours that differ between sources hold it back.

quotes.text: トヨタ自動車グループオフィス。
クリエイティブでイノベイティブで誰もが次の世界を創ろうと思える素晴らしい空間

P73.summaryEn: A 4.0 over 23 reviews; the single sampled review is a glowing note about the creative atmosphere of the Toyota-group space, with nothing on practicalities.

P74.pitch: Cut-price work corner inside an ACCEA print shop by Suidobashi east exit; pay-by-15-minutes desks that suit a quick hour between trains and little else.
order: Free drinks (limited range per one review)
Bring your own food
P74.best: Short bursts only; reviewers say the two web-meeting booths should be booked ahead if you need one, and one advises walking on to the Jimbocho branch for longer work.
P74.workNotes: Outlets at every seat, fast Wi-Fi, two web-meeting booths that are explicitly not soundproof; billing in 15-minute units, printing on site.
P74.headsUp: No toilet even for paying users (the convenience store next door is the workaround); copier and staff noise from the print shop is the recurring complaint, and one reviewer left a booth over sound leakage and poor air-con. Weekend hours conflict between sources; Google says 10:00-19:00.

why.vibe: A 2.0 rating; reviewers describe a cramped office corner with print-shop noise.
why.uniq: A standard ACCEA Cafe formula squeezed into leftover shop space.
why.food: Free drinks are claimed, though one review says the range is thinner than other branches.
why.work: Outlets and Wi-Fi exist, but noise, non-soundproof booths and no toilet make sustained work hard.

quotes.text: ・料金を支払っても、トイレの利用は不可
ワークスペースとは思えないうるささです…
個室は音が漏れ、空調も効かずです。
トイレないけど隣のコンビニで借りられる。

P74.summaryEn: Reviews (2.0, 7) are mostly negative: no toilet, copier and staff noise, leaky booths and weak air-con; the few defenders value the station proximity and low price for short stints.

P75.pitch: Business-Airport lounge in the preserved Kudan Kaikan facing the palace moat; the smartest room in the chain, billed by the half hour, for impressing clients.
order: Free drink bar
Café downstairs (discount for users)
Food trucks outside at lunch
P75.best: Early weekday mornings from 07:00; one reviewer says daytime is always crowded and seats are hard to find. Ground-floor entry, no lift required.
P75.workNotes: Fast Wi-Fi and outlets, web-meeting rooms, phone booths and meeting rooms, monitor loans; 24-hour access is members only.
P75.headsUp: Google lists Saturday closed despite the sheet claim of weekday-plus-Saturday hours. ¥550 per 30 minutes adds up fast; one reviewer found the usage rules fiddly.

why.vibe: Reviewers call it the most luxurious branch in the chain, with the moat and lotus view outside.
why.uniq: A coworking lounge inside a preserved 1930s hall is not something the chain repeats.
why.food: Free drinks inside, with a discounted café downstairs and lunch food trucks.
why.work: Booths, rooms and monitors are excellent, but daytime crowding and the high half-hourly rate are real limits.

quotes.text: すべての拠点で九段が1番ラグジュアリーだと思います。
日中はいつも混んでいるので座る場所を確保するのが困難。
利用ルールが煩雑で使いづらい

P75.summaryEn: Reviews (4.1, 10) rate it the best-looking Business-Airport, clean and well located; the negatives are daytime crowding and rules that one user found cumbersome.

P76.pitch: Independent 7F room between Akihabara and Ochanomizu with a lawn-style shoes-off corner, dual monitors and good free coffee; quiet solo work on a budget.
order: Free coffee (praised)
Paid snacks on the shelf
No water in the drink bar, per one review
P76.best: Open 10:00-18:00 every day, so weekend daytime is the draw; day-pass users can come and go, and the soft chairs and dual-monitor desks get the praise.
P76.workNotes: Wi-Fi and outlets, dual monitors at desks, 30-minute billing for hourly use; registration is a three-minute paper form with cash and e-money accepted, no app or card needed.
P76.headsUp: Closes at 18:00 and reviewers repeatedly wish it stayed open later; one 2023 review complains of loud reception staff. Google files this as Ochanomizu GrinSpace, the same operator as the GrinSpace listing above.

why.vibe: Quiet, plush chairs, a grassy corner with pillows; reviewers describe it as relaxing.
why.uniq: The lawn and shoes-off nap area plus a paper-form, cash-friendly entry are unlike the app-driven chains.
why.food: Free coffee that reviewers rate, plus paid snacks; no meals.
why.work: Monitors, outlets and Wi-Fi at a low rate, but the 18:00 close is the clear limitation.

quotes.text: 静かで快適！椅子もフカフカでした。かなり集中できます。
利用料が安い上に静かで、デュアルモニターを利用できるのが嬉しいです。
丸1日の利用では、自由に出入りする事が可能です。
受付でスタッフが大きい声でずっと話しているので、集中して仕事したい人にはオススメしないです。

P76.summaryEn: Reviews (3.9, 38) praise the quiet, cheap rates, comfy chairs, dual monitors and simple registration; complaints are the 18:00 closing, no water on the drink bar, and one report of noisy reception staff.

P77.pitch: Independent drop-in on 3F of an old building by Akihabara station; monitors on every table and long weekday hours, for travelling workers and small meetings.
order: Free ice pops (chupet)
Drinks: not confirmed
P77.best: Weekdays 07:30-21:00 give the longest run; the morning and evening 3-hour deal at ¥1,100 is the value slot. Weekends 10:00-19:00.
P77.workNotes: Wi-Fi and outlets, external displays on tables, receipts issued, flexible extensions reported; used for both solo work and small group meetings and online streaming.
P77.headsUp: Building is old (rooms are clean); one late-2025 review says the meeting room advertised online is now an office, and another says service has slipped. Separate smoking area on site.

why.vibe: Old building with a university-classroom feel, clean and spacious rather than stylish.
why.uniq: Monitors on every table and a free ice-pop service are a distinct, unfussy idea.
why.food: Nothing beyond free ice pops is confirmed.
why.work: Outlets, Wi-Fi, monitors, meetings tolerated and 07:30-21:00 weekdays cover most needs.

quotes.text: ビル自体古いですが、東京のコワーキングスペースの中でも、かなり使い勝手が良いです。
テーブルごとに外付けモニターが置いてあるところが良い。
ホームページに「会議室あり」とありますが、現在はオフィスになっており使用できませんでした。
駅近以外のメリットない。

P77.summaryEn: Reviews (4.4, 105) like the station proximity, per-table monitors, flexible staff and long weekday hours; the building is dated, the meeting room may no longer exist, and one reviewer feels service has declined.

P78.pitch: Small rental office and coworking room five minutes south of Tachikawa station; weekday-only desks with a joining fee, for locals rather than visitors.
order: Drinks: not confirmed
Bring your own light food (take rubbish away)
P78.best: Weekdays only, 10:00-17:00 per Google, so it is a daytime room; the 2024 reviewer found it clean and comfortable.
P78.workNotes: Wi-Fi, meeting room and multifunction printer; a 2019 review reports VPN connections blocked and no rubbish bins, so carry your waste out.
P78.headsUp: First visit costs an extra ¥1,320 registration. Closed weekends and finishes at 17:00. Several reviews concern the virtual-office post service rather than the desks.

why.vibe: Clean and pleasant per the one drop-in review; 3.6 overall.
why.uniq: A generic small-town shared office.
why.food: No drinks mentioned anywhere.
why.work: A 17:00 close, weekday-only opening, a joining fee and blocked VPN add up to real friction.

quotes.text: ドロップインで利用しました。綺麗で使い勝手よく、居心地良かったです。
・ゴミ箱がありません。軽食は持ち込み可ですが、ゴミは自分で持ち帰る必要があります。
・VPNが制限されています。接続しようとしても繋がりません。

P78.summaryEn: Sparse reviews (3.6, 12): a recent drop-in found it clean with friendly staff; an older one warns of no bins and a blocked VPN; others only concern the mail-forwarding service.

P79.pitch: Coin Space partitioned study floor on 7F of Tachikawa Takashimaya; 07:00-23:00, cheap by the half hour, loved by exam students, not by anyone on Zoom.
order: Nothing provided; bring your own
Department store food floors below
P79.best: Mornings, before the Wi-Fi degrades; one regular recommends the F area for its high ceiling and partition height. Late evenings empty out, which a parent found unnerving.
P79.workNotes: Outlets at desks (some blocked by the desk-lamp plug), partitioned seats and semi-private rooms, meeting rooms, meetings permitted at seats; Wi-Fi measured at 20Mbps at best and under 2Mbps in the afternoon by several reviewers.
P79.headsUp: Do not rely on the Wi-Fi for calls; four separate reviews report Zoom dropping. No bins, no drinks, air-con runs cold. Monthly-plan billing is by emailed link and drew complaints.

why.vibe: Clean and high-ceilinged with good partitions, but a 2.5 rating and a chilly, bin-less room.
why.uniq: A standard Coin Space floor that happens to sit in a department store.
why.food: No drinks at all; bring your own.
why.work: Long hours and outlets, but the repeatedly measured weak Wi-Fi makes online meetings unreliable.

quotes.text: 他の方も書いてますが、とにかく激弱wi-fiです。
午後以降、Wi-Fiの速度が極端に下がります。
ごみを捨てる場所がない。
天井が高く、パーティションの広さや高さ、照明の度合いや雰囲気、席の多さも気に入っていて、自習するのにとても良い場所です。

P79.summaryEn: Reviews (2.5, 29) split between students who value the quiet partitioned desks and long hours, and remote workers furious about Wi-Fi that collapses in the afternoon; no bins, no drinks and cold air-con come up too.

P80.pitch: Kaikatsu CLUB net and manga café on 3-4F by Tachikawa north exit; lockable private booths, drink bar and showers, 24 hours, for naps and heads-down work.
order: Free drink bar (3F only)
No microwave, per one review
P80.best: A Sunday lunchtime visit found it empty; take a 3F booth so the toilets and drink bar are on your floor.
P80.workNotes: Wi-Fi, outlets and lockable private booths with a flat option; showers on site; all booths are private, split over two floors with reception on 3F. Calls in a booth are tolerated by the format but not advertised.
P80.headsUp: Toilets, reception and drinks are only on 3F, and the manga shelves are on 2F, so a 4F booth means stairs for everything. Reviewers find it dearer than other branches with fewer amenities; standard net-café ID registration applies.

why.vibe: A 2.4 rating; clean in the Kaikatsu way but reviewers call the facilities thin and the layout awkward.
why.uniq: One branch of a national net-café chain.
why.food: Drink bar included, nothing else confirmed and no microwave.
why.work: 24-hour private booths with power are useful, but the toilet-on-another-floor layout and pricing grate.

quotes.text: ブースはすべて個室です。3階と4階に、わかれています。受付、トイレ、飲料は3階、4階はブースのみです。
郊外の店舗にしては料金が若干高い事と、設備が乏しい事が挙げられます。
ビジネスマンが移動の合間に静かにofficeを使用して仕事するのには向いていると思いました。

P80.summaryEn: Reviews (2.4, 105) treat it as a place to sleep between trains: private, clean, usually empty, close to the station; complaints are the two-floor layout with toilets and drinks only on 3F, few manga, no microwave and prices high for what is offered.

P81.pitch: Engineer-focused coworking room three minutes from Omotesando run by the software firm anti-pattern; hourly or day desks in an area short of affordable seats.
order: Drinks: not confirmed
P81.best: Hours are 10:00-20:00; nothing else is known, so treat a weekday afternoon as the safe bet.
P81.workNotes: Operator markets it to engineers, which implies Wi-Fi and outlets, but neither is stated in the sheet; no information on booths, calls or registration.
P81.headsUp: No Google listing matched, so facilities and current status are unverified; check the operator site before travelling.

why.vibe: No evidence either way; assumed a clean small office room.
why.uniq: A developer-run space for developers is a clear idea, if unproven here.
why.food: Nothing on drinks or food.
why.work: Reasonable hours and rates, but everything beyond that is unconfirmed.

P81.summaryEn: No recent Google reviews to draw on.

P82.pitch: Nishi-Shimbashi 4F coworking studio with doorless box booths and a few private rooms; long favoured by publishing freelancers, quiet weekday desk work.
order: Drinks: not confirmed
P82.best: Weekdays 10:00-20:00 only; the box booths give a semi-enclosed desk, the private rooms are the option if you need to talk.
P82.workNotes: Wi-Fi and outlets, mix of doorless booths and private rooms; conversation carries between booths and the room expects quiet.
P82.headsUp: Closed weekends. One member reports being warned for a slightly loud discussion and then having their contract ended, so keep calls to a private room.

why.vibe: Clean, bright desks, calm; 4.3 but from only eight reviews, most nearly a decade old.
why.uniq: A small studio with a publishing-industry regulars crowd has a character chains lack.
why.food: No drinks confirmed.
why.work: Outlets and Wi-Fi at a low day rate, but weekend closure and a strict noise culture limit it.

quotes.text: ボックス系（ドア無し）ブースが多い為、話しが筒抜けになる。
静かでとてもよく集中できました。
個室もブースもあるので、仕事のスタイルによって選べます。

P82.summaryEn: Reviews (4.3, 8) are mostly from 2017: clean, quiet, bright desks and a choice of rooms or booths; the one negative says booths leak sound and that raised voices led to a cancelled contract.

P83.pitch: Bare-bones coworking room in Moto-Akasaka priced by the half hour with a ¥1,500 daily ceiling; suits anyone near Akasaka who needs a cheap desk for a full day.
order: Drinks: not confirmed
P83.best: Google gives weekdays 09:00-20:00 and weekends closed; the sheet claims 24-hour use, which is more likely a members-only key.
P83.workNotes: Wi-Fi and outlets claimed; nothing known about booths, calls or registration.
P83.headsUp: Two Google reviews and none sampled, so everything here is from the operator; the 24-hour claim conflicts with listed hours.

why.vibe: A 3.5 from two reviews and no description; assume a plain office room.
why.uniq: Nothing distinctive beyond the low daily cap.
why.food: No drinks mentioned.
why.work: Outlets, Wi-Fi and a ¥1,500 cap are good value, but hours are unclear and weekends closed.

P83.summaryEn: No recent Google reviews to draw on.

P84.pitch: fabbit shared office on 7F near Ginza-itchome with big glass windows and a staffed reception; day pass with free drinks, quieter than other fabbit floors.
order: Free drink bar
Lunch options nearby are limited, per one review
P84.best: Weekday daytime with the window seats; a long-term user says the free seats are noticeably emptier than Aoyama or Otemachi.
P84.workNotes: Wi-Fi, free drinks, staff on site during 09:00-18:00 weekdays, web meetings reported without trouble; 24-hour access in the claims applies to members, not day-pass holders.
P84.headsUp: Reception hours are weekdays only. Not station-connected, so the walk is exposed in rain. Bicycles can be left in the shared area by the lifts.

why.vibe: Natural light through large windows and a receptionist reviewers keep praising.
why.uniq: A well-kept but typical fabbit floor.
why.food: Free drinks; nothing to eat on site and few lunch spots nearby.
why.work: Comfortable and calm with Wi-Fi and staff, but weekday-only opening for visitors.

quotes.text: 比較的空いている（青山や大手町に比べてフリー席は静かです）
外出先でウェブ会議にでたくて利用しました。管理の方が常駐されているので安心。
コスパ良くて快適な空間

P84.summaryEn: Reviews (4.3, 21) are warm: clean, bright, affordable, an exceptional receptionist and free seats that stay quiet; minor gripes are few lunch options and an awkward wet-weather walk from the station.

P85.pitch: Entre Salon’s flagship Ginza reception; half-hourly drop-in valid at every branch in Tokyo, Kanagawa and Saitama, popular with small-business networkers.
order: Drinks: not confirmed
P85.best: Saturdays are reported quieter than weekdays; the 8F lounge has window-side meeting tables and is calmer than the Ikebukuro branch. Weekdays 09:00-21:00, Saturday to 18:00.
P85.workNotes: Wi-Fi and outlets claimed; open lounge with plenty of meeting tables, meeting and seminar rooms bookable, several buildings share the one reception.
P85.headsUp: Closed Sundays. One source says drop-in is not offered, contradicting the operator; confirm at reception. Only one toilet in building 1, nearest convenience store is a walk, and networking events can fill the lounge.

why.vibe: Clean, roomy and quiet for its main-road address, if plainly office-like.
why.uniq: The all-branch pass and the events-and-introductions culture set it apart from desk-only chains.
why.food: No drinks mentioned in claims or reviews.
why.work: Outlets, Wi-Fi and long weekday hours, but Sunday closure, one toilet and event crowds intrude.

quotes.text: 最近、土曜日の利用が多く、普段より空いています。
８階ということもあり、大通り沿いですが静かです。
トイレが1つしかなかったので最低でも2つあると嬉しいなと思いました。
交流会の参加者が多くて賑わっています。

P85.summaryEn: Reviews (4.6, 89) praise the clean, spacious rooms, easy bookings and the networking events where people meet collaborators; the recurring niggles are a single toilet, a walk to the nearest convenience store and busy event days.
